questions.prompt: An operating system is usually designed to run on any of a class of machines, so it must be configured for each specific site.
What is the name of the program that obtains information about a specific hardware configuration? (one word)
Which is something SYSGEN needs to find out?
options: How much memory the machine has

questions.prompt: What can SYSGEN's information be used to build?
Why can a system-specific kernel be more efficient than a general one?
options: It includes only what this machine needs, so it can generate more efficient code

questions.prompt: With a custom-compiled kernel, changing the hardware may mean rebuilding the kernel.
How do most modern desktop systems handle different hardware?
options: One general kernel that detects hardware at boot and loads the modules it needs
Running SYSGEN every time a key is pressed
They only support one exact computer model
A different hand-written OS for every computer
